newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia president announces election for Nov 10.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia president announces election for Nov 10.

text.p: Slovenian President Milan Kucan on Thursday set November 10 as the date of the former Yugoslav republic's next general election.
The poll will be Slovenia's third multi-party election and the second since the country declared independence from former Yugoslavia in June 1991.
"I have just signed a decree announcing general elections for November 10, 1996," Kucan told a news conference.
Kucan, a former communist, said he had made the decision after talking to the leaders of most political parties currently represented in the 90-seat lower house of parliament.
The centrist Liberal Democrats of Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek, currently ahead in opinion polls, were known to favour November 10 as the election date.
The main opposition rightist Social Democrats had urged Kucan to delay the election until a court ruling on whether a referendum should be held on electoral reform.
Slovenia, which borders Italy, Austria and Croatia, has one of the most successful economies among ex-communist states in central and eastern Europe.
But Drnovsek's government was forced to relax tight monetary controls during the election year following a number of protracted strikes in the public sector.

The small, Alpine nation has won plaudits in the West for setting up a solid democracy and developing a free market economy. It is likely to be included in the first wave of new members to join NATO next year and has made a formal application for membership of the European Union.
